blocks.body:
# Spatial Mesh & LoRa connection

Spatial Mesh is the TacNav radio screen for **LoRa / Meshtastic** messaging, node tracking, and map sharing. It appears when the **Spatial Mesh plugin** (`com.myspatial.meshtastic`) is installed. The plugin owns the single Bluetooth link to the radio; MiliNav is the soldier UI.

The map still works without the plugin. The mesh shortcut and **Tools → Plugins → Spatial Mesh** stay hidden until the plugin package is present.

> Install MiliNav and the plugin from the **same update** so the AIDL binder matches. Close the stock Meshtastic app before connecting — a radio allows **one** Bluetooth link.

## Quick visual

![Spatial Mesh architecture](/media/diagrams/mesh-architecture.svg)

**In this project**

| Piece | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `mesh-api` module | AIDL contract (`ISpatialMesh` / `IMeshClient`) |
| `SpatialMeshClient` | Bind / connect / send / radio config |
| `SpatialMeshSession` | Host state: chat, tracks, receipts, radio edits |
| `SpatialMeshConsole` | Soldier UI tabs (Chat, Nodes, Channels, Setup, …) |
| `SpatialMeshMapLayer` | Markers and trails on TacMap |
| Plugin package | `com.myspatial.meshtastic` |

## Setup (soldier steps)

![Spatial Mesh setup flow](/media/diagrams/mesh-setup-flow.svg)

1. Install **MiliNav** and the **Spatial Mesh** plugin from the same release.
2. Open TacNav → tap the **mesh** icon (or **Tools → Plugins → Spatial Mesh**).
3. Turn **Enable** on. Allow Bluetooth and notifications if asked.
4. Wait until the status chip says the radio is **linked** (top icon turns **green**).
5. Open the **Setup** tab: set long/short name, range/hops, channels, location options.
6. Press **Save to radio** once. Wait through **Saving → Restarting → Checking → Saved**.
7. For region, Wi‑Fi password, Bluetooth PIN, MQTT server, firmware, or factory reset: press **Release**, do that in the Meshtastic app, close Meshtastic, then **Connect** again.

**PIN tip:** if Android asks for a Bluetooth PIN, try `123456`.

### Icon colours

| Colour | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Amber | Plugin installed, mesh off |
| Green | Radio Bluetooth link up |
| Red | Mesh on but link dropped (toast on link drop) |

## How data travels

![How mesh data travels](/media/diagrams/mesh-data-path.svg)

End-to-end path:

1. Soldier types chat or shares a map graphic in **TacNav**.
2. Host calls the plugin over **AIDL** (`sendText` / `sendWaypoint`, …).
3. Plugin talks to the radio over **Bluetooth**.
4. Radio encrypts (channel PSK when configured) and transmits on **LoRa**.
5. Other radios may **rebroadcast** up to the hop limit (usually 3, range 1–7).
6. Peer radios decrypt and hand packets to their plugins → peer TacNav UI / map.

### Node travel (hop / bounce)

LoRa mesh does **not** open a phone-style call. Your radio **broadcasts** a packet. Nearby radios that hear it may **repeat** it so nodes farther away can receive it. Each repeat is one **hop** (also called a **bounce**).

![Node hop / bounce limit](/media/diagrams/mesh-node-hops.svg)

**Typical path on the air**

1. **You** send → plugin → your LoRa radio.
2. Radios in RF range hear the packet.
3. If hops remain, a peer **rebroadcasts** (Node A → Node B → …).
4. When **remaining hops = 0**, nodes stop repeating that packet.
5. The destination (or the whole channel, for public) shows the message in TacNav.

### Maximum hops to reach a user

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Where | **Setup → Range and speed → Hop limit** |
| Typical default | **3** |
| Allowed in TacNav | **1 – 7** |

- Hop limit = **maximum number of times** other nodes may rebroadcast that packet.
- With hop limit **3**: roughly You → A → B → Target (three relays). A farther 4th bounce does **not** happen for that packet.
- Hop limit is **not** radio metres. **Modem preset** (e.g. Long Fast) sets RF reach of one radio; hops set how many **node bounces** are allowed after that.
- Raise hops (4–7) when the team needs many mid-path relays and you accept more airtime. Keep hops low (1–2) for dense, short-range teams.
- If a private peer is beyond hop reach, status may stay **Queued / Retrying** — move closer, place a mid-path node, or raise hop limit.

## Public (channel) vs private (direct)

In Meshtastic / Spatial Mesh there is no separate “public_channel” type name. Routing is decided by **`toId`** on the same channel index:

![Public vs private node travel](/media/diagrams/mesh-public-private-flow.svg)

| Mode | How you start it | Who sees the chat | How it travels |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Public / channel** | Channel → **Everyone on this channel** | All nodes with that channel PSK | Flood: decrypt **and** rebroadcast until hops run out |
| **Private / direct** | Node → **Send message** | Only the addressed peer (DM thread) | Same LoRa channel; other nodes may **relay** but do not open a DM |

![Channel broadcast vs private direct](/media/diagrams/mesh-channels.svg)

### Channel broadcast — “Everyone on this channel”

- UI: pick a channel → send to **Everyone on this channel**.
- API: `sendText(message, channelIndex, hopLimit, toId="")` — empty `toId`.
- Session labels the thread as `ch N` (`direct = false`).
- Anyone with the **channel PSK** (and matching LoRa settings) can read it.
- Delivery status typically stays **Sent** (no end-to-end delivery ACK for broadcast).
- Node travel: every hearing member may show the chat **and** bounce the packet while hops remain.

Think of this as the **shared / “public on this net”** lane for that channel name (Primary, Secondary, …).

### Private / direct message

- UI: open a node → **Send message**, or pick a peer in chat.
- API: same `channelIndex`, but `toId` set to the peer node id (e.g. `!abcd1234`).
- Plugin chat `kind == "direct"`; session key `d:peerId`.
- Other mesh members still hear RF and may **relay** it (same hop limit), but only the addressed peer opens a DM thread.
- Status can move **Queued → Delivered** (routing reply NONE), or **Retrying** (one private retry).

> Private is “addressed”, not a separate radio network. Relays can still burn airtime; they just do not show someone else’s DM.

### Encryption and keys

- Channel **PSK** is written once via Setup / `addChannel(..., psk, ...)` and **never shown again** in TacNav (`hasKey` only).
- Roles: **PRIMARY** / **SECONDARY** / **DISABLED**. Disabled slots are hidden. Slot **0** cannot be removed.
- **LOC on** = channel role not disabled **and** `positionPrecision > 0` → that channel may share radio GPS for the map.

## Chat, location, and map share

![Message delivery states](/media/diagrams/mesh-delivery.svg)

- Message box: **250 characters**, at most **231 UTF-8 bytes**.
- **Share location** in a conversation sends this phone’s GPS **once** as a chat line — it does not start a repeating broadcast, and that line is not drawn as a track.
- The **T-Beam (radio)** sends its own position when location sharing is configured. TacNav does **not** timer-broadcast phone GPS from Setup.
- A radio marker appears only when **Show** is on for that node **and** the fix arrived on a channel that shares location.
- Share drawings/markers from the **radial menu** → choose a channel or a direct radio (waypoints + optional corner packets).

## Channels & Setup groups (reference)

Setup groups (tap a section, then **Save to radio** once):

1. **Radio details** (read-only: region, modem, frequency, …)
2. **Range and speed** — modem preset, hop limit, boost / MQTT filters
3. **Location sharing** — GPS interval, smart position, extra fields
4. **This radio** — role, rebroadcast, power, screen (Router/Repeater need confirm)
5. **Message channels** — edit/add channel (name ≤ 12 bytes; paste PSK once)
6. **Extra features** — telemetry, store & forward, MQTT module switch, …
7. **Clock and radios** — set radio clock from phone; remove another node

## Library, KML, battle graphics

- **Library → LoRa tracking** — saved radio paths; **Export** to `.kml`
- **Layers → Import KML** — bring tracks back onto the map
- **Share battle graphics** — optional checkbox for LoRa tracks, markers, and drawings (does not re-inject into the live radio list)
